title: What If The Sun Forgot To Rise?

publish.title: What If The Sun FORGOT To Rise? #shorts
publish.description: What if one morning the sun simply did not show up, and the night just kept going? Would you sleep in or go wake it up?
publish.caption: What if the sun forgot to rise? 🌙☀️

scenes.line: What if the sun just *forgot* to rise?
scenes.title: WHAT IF...

scenes.line: My alarm rang at seven. Outside, it was still *midnight*.
Mom checked the clock. Then the window. Then the clock *again*.
The news said: the sun is *late*. Please stay calm.
No sun meant no school. Best news *ever*.
We played tag under a giant *moon*.
Zoe sold glow sticks. She made a *fortune*.
Then the sky turned *green*. Grandpa said that was new.
Day two. Still *night*. It stopped being funny.
The flowers closed. The birds went *quiet*.
Everyone was sleepy all the time. Even the *dogs*.
Max asked if the sun was *mad* at us.
Day three. The moon turned *red*.
Okay. Somebody had to go *wake* it up.
I climbed the tallest building in *town*.
I yelled good morning. *Nothing*.
I banged a pot. I played a trumpet. *Badly*.
I even told it a *joke*. The sun did not laugh.
Then I remembered something Grandpa always *says*.
Nobody wakes up for someone who only *complains*.
We yelled at the sun every *day*. Too hot. Too bright.
So this time I just said *thank* you.
For the beach days. For the long *summers*.
Then Zoe said it. Then Max. Then the whole *town*.
And slowly, the sky turned *pink*.
The sun came up. Three days late. Looking *embarrassed*.
It turns out the sun just wanted one day *off*.
So now, every year, the sun gets a *holiday*.
One whole day of night. We call it Thank You *Day*.
Zoe still sells the glow sticks. Of *course* she does.
